course_name_original: Embedded Systems Programming and Applications in the Environment (5401ELE)
course_name_en: Embedded Systems Programming and Applications in the Environment

learning_outcomes.text: Define electronic circuit operations and design
Design, analyse and implement finite state machine based digital circuits
Describe and identify suitable interfaces for modern microcontroller/embedded systems
Select appropriate hardware, software platforms and interface considering power, cost and capability requirements
Produce integrated embedded systems with external sensors and actuators

syllabus_topics: Review of Boolean algebra and Karnaugh maps
Counter Design Synchronous sequential state machine design and analysis, including Mealy, Moore and mixed type circuits
Identify the advantages and disadvantages of various processors available on the market
Research the costs of mass production identifying the power and capability of the devices
Plan for the power requirements of embedded systems, considering different use case requirements in real-life applications
Create embedded systems that interface with various sensors, both analogue and digital, ensuring that inputs are buffered to protect the processor from hazardous conditions
Integrate processors with control devices e.g. Arduinos, Servos, DC Motors, etc.

assessment_methods.method: Portfolio (Digital and embedded System CW demo, viva and report)

institution: Liverpool John Moores University — BEng (Hons) Electrical and Electronic Engineering
